items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Dodgion’s saxophone playing, influenced by that of Charlie Parker, Art Pepper and Jerome Richardson

ctx.x: then we went on, and we were not sitting close together. And after the first — we played the first tune and Bob Brookmeyer sitting behind me I hear him say, “I told you you guys couldn’t play outside of the Vanguard. It sounds terrible.” So we had everybody sit closer together. So we sat closer together like we did at the Vanguard and then the band started to sound better again. It was really funny. It was great.

I want to read something that was written about you in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz. See if you think that this guy knows what he’s talking about. He says: “Dodgion’s saxophone playing, influenced by that of Charlie Parker, Art Pepper and Jerome Richardson, is well represented by his inventive solo on ‘Tip Toe,’ which draws on blues formulas and demonstrates a relaxed rhythmic sense and the ability to develop motifs.”
Gee that’s pretty formal I guess.
